title: Farmer Onboarding KYC
summary: Onboard farmers and FPO members from phone photos of KYC, bank and land documents, with masked Aadhaar, name matching across scripts, duplicate checks and consent captured in their language.

seo.title: Farmer Onboarding KYC with AI | VipraTech
seo.description: AI farmer onboarding: reads KYC, bank and land documents from field photos, masks Aadhaar, matches names across scripts and flags duplicates for review.

problem.intro: Field agents onboard farmers at village meetings and collection points, photographing ID cards, bank passbooks and land records on their phones. Back-office teams then fix blurred photos, retype names written in Hindi and English, and chase missing documents, while the farmer waits weeks for membership, input credit or payments.

pain_points.title: Poor photos from the field
pain_points.detail: Glare, cropped edges and blurred passbook pages mean documents are often rejected days after the visit.

pain_points.title: Names in different scripts
pain_points.detail: The same farmer appears in Devanagari on a land record, in English on a bank passbook, and with another spelling on a voter ID.

pain_points.title: Duplicate registrations
pain_points.detail: Farmers registered by different agents, FPOs or programmes create duplicate records and double benefits or credit.

pain_points.title: Consent that is hard to evidence
pain_points.detail: Consent forms in English, signed without explanation, do not show the farmer understood how their data will be used.

solution.overview: We build an onboarding flow for field agent apps and back offices. As the agent photographs each document, the app checks the image is sharp and complete and asks for a retake on the spot. The pipeline classifies documents, extracts fields, masks Aadhaar numbers immediately and keeps only what your process needs. Names are matched across scripts with transliteration-aware comparison, and bank details can be confirmed with a penny-drop check through your payment provider. A duplicate check compares each new farmer with existing records by name, father's name, village, mobile and bank account. Consent is read out in the farmer's language and recorded. Mismatches and possible duplicates go to a KYC reviewer.
capabilities: On-device photo quality checks with retake prompts for field agents
Document classification and field extraction for ID, bank and land documents
Aadhaar masking before anything is stored
Transliteration-aware name matching across Devanagari, regional scripts and English
Duplicate farmer detection across agents, FPOs and programmes
Consent notice read out in the farmer's language, with recorded acknowledgement

workflow.title: Capture in the field
workflow.detail: The field agent photographs documents in the app, which checks quality and asks for retakes immediately.

workflow.title: Record consent
workflow.detail: The app plays a consent notice in the farmer's language and records the acknowledgement.

workflow.title: Extract and mask
workflow.detail: Fields are extracted, Aadhaar is masked, and only the data your process needs is kept.

workflow.title: Match and de-duplicate
workflow.detail: Names and details are matched across documents and against existing farmer records.

workflow.title: KYC reviewer decision
workflow.detail: Mismatches, possible duplicates and low-confidence fields go to a reviewer who approves, corrects or requests documents.

workflow.title: Activate the farmer
workflow.detail: Approved farmers are created in your CRM or ERP and notified by SMS or WhatsApp.

inputs: Photos of masked Aadhaar, voter ID or PAN
outputs: Verified farmer profile with masked identifiers
Name match and duplicate check results
human_in_the_loop: KYC reviewers decide every name mismatch, possible duplicate and low-confidence document. Where onboarding feeds a regulated loan, the lender's KYC team applies its own policy before any account is opened.
integrations: Payment provider for bank account verification
SMS gateway or WhatsApp Business API
DigiLocker, where your use case permits
guardrails: Aadhaar masked before storage and handled per UIDAI rules
Data minimisation: only the fields your process needs are kept
Possible duplicates never auto-merged; a reviewer confirms
Consent notice versioned and linked to each record
compliance_notes: Consent capture and purpose limitation designed in line with the DPDP Act 2023, with notices in the farmer's language.
For regulated lenders, the flow is designed to feed, not replace, customer due diligence under the RBI KYC Master Direction.

pilot.scope: Onboarding for one FPO or one district's field team, with documents captured in the app and reviewed in parallel with the current process.
deliverables: Field capture flow with quality checks

faqs.a: No. Aadhaar is masked as soon as it is read, and only the masked form is stored, in line with UIDAI rules. Where your process needs Aadhaar-based verification, it goes through an authorised route.

faqs.q: Will it work without network in villages?
faqs.a: Yes. The app checks photo quality on the phone and queues documents offline, syncing when the agent reaches coverage.

faqs.q: How do you match names written in different scripts?
faqs.a: We transliterate and compare names using rules tuned for Indian names, alongside father's name, village and mobile number. Close matches go to a reviewer rather than being merged automatically.

faqs.q: Can farmers give consent if they cannot read?
faqs.a: Yes. The consent notice is played as audio in their language, and their acknowledgement is recorded with the agent present. The record is linked to the farmer's profile.
